name: GlassesSA
shortDescription: A South Australian Government program providing low-cost prescription glasses and, for eligible serious eye conditions, no-cost contact lenses.
plainEnglishSummary: If you have an eligible concession card or meet another eligibility pathway, GlassesSA may help you obtain low-cost prescription glasses. People with certain serious eye conditions may receive prescribed contact lenses at no cost.
audience: South Australian residents holding an eligible concession card
Children and young people in state care
Dependants of people eligible for standard glasses
People with a prescribed serious eye condition requiring contact lenses
supportTypes: No-cost contact lenses for prescribed serious eye conditions
availabilityNote: Eligible customers can generally receive one new pair of glasses every three years, or earlier when clinically necessary. Maximum customer payments for standard glasses are $25 for single vision, $30 for single vision grind, $50 for bi-focal and $100 for multi-focal glasses. Eligible Aboriginal customers can receive standard glasses at no cost. Eligible contact lenses are supplied at no cost. Optional upgrades may cost extra.
eligibilityNote: Community Connect cannot confirm eligibility. Applicants generally need to live in South Australia and hold an eligible concession card or qualify through another recognised pathway. Contact lenses require a prescribed serious eye condition and must be supplied through an authorised hospital or optometrist.
